text:
### Definition of Terms

DEFINITION OF TERMS

| Term - definition |
| --- |
| Affect - observable emotional response seen in the person’s non-verbal behavior. |
| Delusions - Irrational, strong beliefs which have no basis in reality but which cannot be changed by logic or argument. |
| Disability – refers to any impairment which may be physical, mental, and developmental or a combination of these. |
| Fear - The body’s physiologic and emotional response to a known or recognized danger. |
| Flight of ideas – is a symptom that is common in BAD mania patients manifested by expressing many ideas at the same time (jumping from topic to topic). |
| Grandiose delusions – abnormal fixed beliefs of expansive ideas such as inflated worth, power, knowledge, identity or special relationship to a famous person. |
| Hallucinations - perceptions that occur in the absence of any appropriate external stimuli and could be of any of the five senses. |
| Illusion - a false interpretation or perception of a real environmental stimulus that may involve any of the five senses. |
| Insomnia – inability to sleep well either difficulty in initiating and/or maintaining sleep or interrupted sleeping pattern. |
| Impulsivity - behavior characterized by little or no forethought, reflection, or consideration of the consequences. |
| Mental Status Examination (MSE) - a structured way of observing and describing a patient’s current state of mind under the domains of appearance, attitude, behavior, mood, speech, thought process, thought content, perception, cognitions, judgment and insight |
| Mood - a normal internal felt subjective emotion that a person experiences most of the time. |
| Psychotherapy - use of psychological methods based on regular personal interaction to help a person change and overcome problems in desired ways. It aims at increasing each individual’s wellbeing and mental health. |
| Psychosis - A term that refers to a patient presenting with hallucinations, and/or delusions and/or illusions. |
| Tolerance: is a state where by the individual who uses alcohol and/or drugs feels the need for markedly increased amounts of the substance to achieve intoxication. |
| Withdrawal: are symptoms that occur upon abrupt cessation of excessive alcohol/ substance use. |
| Dependence: is an adaptive state that develops when an individual persist in use of alcohol/ substance despite problems related to the use of the substance. |

Diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder | MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER WITH SUICIDAL THOUGHTS OR ATTEMPT, NO PSYCHOSIS | • Conduct a Suicidal Risk Assessment Go to page 99 • Assess criteria for inpatient care • Initiate antidepressants or refer Go to page 58 • PLUS a sedative if insomnia is one of the presenting symptom preferably Lorazepam 1-2mg nocte for 7/7 • Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy • Adherence counseling Go to page 81 • Family involvement Go to page 81 | | If the patient has;

One or more of the following symptoms improving in the post menses:
- Hallucinations
- Marked mood lability
- Marked irritability or anger
- Marked depressed mood, hopelessness or guilty feeling
With one or more additional symptoms:
- Decreased interest/ pleasure
- Poor concentration
- Marked lack of energy/ lethargy
- Marked change in appetite
- Hypersomnia or insomnia
- A sense of being overwhelmed
- Physical menstrual symptoms; breast tenderness or swelling, joint or muscle pains, sensation of bloating | PREMENSTRUAL DYSPHORIC DISORDER | - Consider above interventions for Major Depressive Disorder, with no suicidality/psychosis
- If there is no improvement with antidepressants and psychotherapy, initiate combined oestrogen-progestin contraceptives or refer | | If the client has:
Prominent and persistent depressed mood or lack of interest/ pleasure, with evidence

Prominent and persistent depressed mood or lack of interest/ pleasure with evidence;
• from history, physical exams or laboratory findings that the disturbance is the direct consequences of a medical condition

• Persistent irritable mood most of the day | DISRUPTIVE MOOD DYSREGULATION DISORDER
(N.B The diagnosis should not be done before age 6 or after 18 years) |

• Provide psychoeducation

• Provide counseling or refer

heading_path: Chapter 3: Overview of Different Psychiatric Conditions > Major Depressive Disorder > Table 2: Stepwise Management of Major Depressive Disorders
text:
### TABLE 2: STEPWISE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS

**Step 1: Community Clinic Level**

| Entry point | Management |
| --- | --- |
| - Mild symptoms of Major Depressive Disorder - No psychosis symptoms - No suicide attempt/thoughts - Stable depression on treatment (continuation phase) | - Take vital signs - Provide health education and support - Encourage family support - Provide counselling - Conduct MSE and physical examinations - Take vital signs - Assess side effects of medications - Assess adherence to medications - Refill medications as indicated - Refer to doctor led services every 6 months for review If not improved within 2 months go to step 2 |

**Step 2: General Hospital or Health Centre**

| Entry point | Management |
| --- | --- |
| - Moderate form of Major Depressive Disorder - Presence of psychosis and suicide thoughts/attempt - Failure at step 1 | - Take vital signs - Conduct MSE and physical examination each visit - Assess side effects and adherence of medications - Provide health education and encourage family support - Initiate or review medications as indicated - Conduct Suicidal Risk Assessment - Assess the need for inpatient care - Counselling If not improved after 2 months go to step 3 |

**Step 3: Specialized Psychiatric Hospital**

| Entry point | Management |
| --- | --- |
| - Failure at step 2. - Children with Major Depressive Disorder - Elderly, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers with any form of Major Depressive Disorder - Severe form of Major Depressive Disorder with or without psychosis or suicidality - Suicide attempt regardless of the severity of Major Depressive Disorder | - Doctor led services - Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy |

text:
### TABLE 3: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF ANXIETY DISORDERS TABLE 3: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF ANXIETY DISORDERS | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has:
- Excessive fear or worry occurring more days for at least 6/12
- Difficult to control the worry
PLUS
3 or more of the following symptoms (NB: in children only 1 item/symptom is required).
- restlessness or feeling keyed up
- easy fatigue,
- difficulty concentrating,
- irritability,
- muscle tension
- insomnia
NB; It must eliminate or exclude drug abuse, medication, medical conditions or other mental disorders that may induce anxiety. | GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER | - Assess and provide counselling or refer
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Prescribe antidepressants or refer (Refer to page 61)
- Consider an anxiolytic to patients presenting with insomnia or in distress | | If the patient has
- Unexpected abrupt surge of intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within a minute
PLUS
4 or more of the following symptoms
- Awareness of heart beats
- Difficulty concentrating
- Sweating
- Trembling or shaking
- Sensation of shortness of breath
- Feelings of choking
- Chest pain or discomfort
- Chills or fever/heat sensations
- Nausea and/or abdominal. discomfort
- numbness or tingling sensations (paresthesias)
- Derealisation or depersonalization
- Fear of losing control/going crazy
- Fear of dying
PLUS
At least one of the attacks has been followed by one month or more of one or both of the following;
- Persistent worry or concern over another attack or their consequences
- Notable change in behaviour related to the attacks
N;B The disturbances are not due to physiological effects drugs of abuse, medications, another mental disorder or medical conditions e.g. hyperthyroidism, cardiopulmonary disorders | PANIC DISORDER | - Provide counselling or refer
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Prescribe antidepressants or refer (Refer to page 61)
- Consider prescribing an anxiolytic to patients presenting with insomnia or in distress | 'Refer to page N' arrows refer to the guide's printed page numbers.

text:

- Conduct MSE and physical examinations
- Assess side effects and adherence of medications
- Provide health education and support
- Encourage family support
- Counselling
- Prescribe/review medications as indicated
If no improvement within two months go to step 3 | **Step 3: National Psychiatric Referral Hospital** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Failure at step 2
- Severe symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder or Panic Disorder
- Children
- Frail elderly
- Pregnant women and breast feeding mothers | - Provide clinical care as indicated
- Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy |

heading_path: Chapter 3: Overview of Different Psychiatric Conditions > Trauma and Stressor Related Disorders > Table 5: Summary of Classification and Management of Trauma and Stressor Related Disorders
text:
### TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS | SIGNS | CLASSIFIED AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | The following are diagnostic criteria;
A. If the patient was exposed to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence in one or more of the following ways;
- Directly experienced the trauma
- Witnessed the event(s) as it occurred to others
- Learned the event(s) occurred to a close relative or friend
- Experienced repeated or extreme exposure to a traumatic event(s) (does not apply to exposure through electronic media, TV, movies, pictures unless the exposure is work related)
Duration of symptoms (criteria B,C, D and E) is more than one month.
B. Presence of one or more of the following symptoms:
- Recurrent involuntary and intrusive distressing memories of traumatic event(s). (in children repetitive play may occur in which themes or aspects of the traumatic event(s) are expressed.
- Recurrent distressing dreams of the traumatic event(s). In children there may be frightening dreams.
- Flash backs of the event(s)
- Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to cues that symbolizes or resembles the traumatic event(s)
- Marked physiological reactions to cues that symbolizes or resembles the traumatic event(s)
C. Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event(s) as evidenced by one or both of the following;
- Avoidance of or efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts or feelings about or associated with the traumatic event(s)
- Avoidance of or efforts to avoid external reminders (such as people, places, objects, activities, situations) about or associated with the traumatic event(s)
D. Negative alterations in cognitions and mood associated with the traumatic event(s) as evidenced by two or more of the following;
- Inability to remember an important aspect of the event
- Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others or the world e.g. I am bad
- Self-blame or blaming others
- Persistent negative emotional state (fear, horror, anger, shame, guilty).
- Lack of interest
- Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.
- Persistent inability to express positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction
E. Marked alterations in an arousal or reactivity associated with the traumatic event as evidenced by two of more of the following;
- Irritability or anger outburst
- Reckless or self-destructive behavior
- Hypervigilance
- Exaggerated startle response
- Problems with concentration
- Sleep disturbances | POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) | - Assess and provide counseling
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Prescribe medications or refer (Refer to Table 26, Page 61)
- Rule out MDD, GAD & Panic Disorder | | - Diagnostic criteria is the similar to PTSD symptoms – but symptoms lasts from 3 days to 1 month following exposure to a traumatic event(s)
- Therefore the diagnosis changes to PTSD if symptoms persists after a month | ACUTE STRESS DISORDER | - Assess and provide counseling
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Provide supportive medications as indicated | | A. Presence of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor(s) occurring within 3 months of the onset of the stressor.
B. These symptoms or behaviors are clinically significant as evidenced by one or both of the following;
- Marked distress that is out of proportion to the severity of the stressor
- Significant impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning
The stress related disturbance does not meet the diagnosis of any other mental illness or normal bereavement | Adjustment disorder | - Assess and provide counseling
- Reassure |

text:
### TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS | SIGNS | CLASSIFIED AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | The following are diagnostic criteria;
A. If the patient was exposed to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence in one or more of the following ways;
- Directly experienced the trauma
- Witnessed the event(s) as it occurred to others
- Learned the event(s) occurred to a close relative or friend
- Experienced repeated or extreme exposure to a traumatic event(s) (does not apply to exposure through electronic media, TV, movies, pictures unless the exposure is work related)
Duration of symptoms (criteria B,C, D and E) is more than one month.
B. Presence of one or more of the following symptoms:
- Recurrent involuntary and intrusive distressing memories of traumatic event(s). (in children repetitive play may occur in which themes or aspects of the traumatic event(s) are expressed.
- Recurrent distressing dreams of the traumatic event(s). In children there may be frightening dreams.
- Flash backs of the event(s)
- Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to cues that symbolizes or resembles the traumatic event(s)
- Marked physiological reactions to cues that symbolizes or resembles the traumatic event(s)
C. Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event(s) as evidenced by one or both of the following;
- Avoidance of or efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts or feelings about or associated with the traumatic event(s)
- Avoidance of or efforts to avoid external reminders (such as people, places, objects, activities, situations) about or associated with the traumatic event(s)
D. Negative alterations in cognitions and mood associated with the traumatic event(s) as evidenced by two or more of the following;
- Inability to remember an important aspect of the event
- Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others or the world e.g. I am bad
- Self-blame or blaming others
- Persistent negative emotional state (fear, horror, anger, shame, guilty).
- Lack of interest
- Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.
- Persistent inability to express positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction
E. Marked alterations in an arousal or reactivity associated with the traumatic event as evidenced by two of more of the following;
- Irritability or anger outburst
- Reckless or self-destructive behavior
- Hypervigilance
- Exaggerated startle response
- Problems with concentration
- Sleep disturbances | POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) | - Assess and provide counseling
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Prescribe medications or refer (Refer to Table 26, Page 61)
- Rule out MDD, GAD & Panic Disorder | | - Diagnostic criteria is the similar to PTSD symptoms – but symptoms lasts from 3 days to 1 month following exposure to a traumatic event(s)
- Therefore the diagnosis changes to PTSD if symptoms persists after a month | ACUTE STRESS DISORDER | - Assess and provide counseling
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Provide supportive medications as indicated | | A. Presence of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor(s) occurring within 3 months of the onset of the stressor.
B. These symptoms or behaviors are clinically significant as evidenced by one or both of the following;
- Marked distress that is out of proportion to the severity of the stressor
- Significant impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning
The stress related disturbance does not meet the diagnosis of any other mental illness or normal bereavement | Adjustment disorder | - Assess and provide counseling
- Reassure |

heading_path: Chapter 3: Overview of Different Psychiatric Conditions > Grief and Bereavement > Table 8: Summary of classification of grief and bereavement
text:
### Table 8: Summary of classification and classification of grief and bereavement | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If an individual experienced the death of someone with a close relationship
PLUS at least one of the following symptoms to a clinically significant degree and has persisted for at least 12 moths;
• Persistent yearning/longing for the deceased
• Intense sorrow and emotional pain in response to the death
• Preoccupation with the deceased
• Preoccupation with the circumstances of the death
PLUS at least six of the following symptoms;
• Marked difficult in accepting death
• Experiencing disbelief or emotional numbness over the loss
• Difficulty with positive reminiscing about the deceased
• Bitterness or anger related to the loss
• Maladaptive appraisals about oneself in relation to the deceased or the death
• Excessive avoidance of reminders of the loss
• A desire to die in order to be with the deceased
• Difficulty trusting other individuals since the death
• Feeling alone or detached from others since the death.
• Feeling life is meaningless or empty without the deceased
• Confusion about one's role in life or a diminished sense of one's identity
• Difficulty or reluctance to pursue interests since the loss or plan for the future | PERSISTENT COMPLEX BEREAVEMENT DISORDER | • Refer or provide the following interventions;
• Support and counselling
• Assess for symptoms of Major Depressive Disorder
• Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counselling. |

- Adherence counseling (Refer page 81)
- Family involvement (Refer page 81)
- Counseling on alcohol and substance use issues | Table 11 continues over pp.41-43 (hypomanic episode, major depressive episode, Bipolar II); see the next item. Page references are the guide's printed page numbers.

text:
### TABLE 12: STEPWISE MANAGEMENT OF BIPOLAR I AND II DISORDERS **Step 1: Community Clinic Level** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Mentally stable Bipolar I Disorder on treatment
- Mentally stable Bipolar II Disorder on treatment | - Take vital signs
- Conduct physical examination and MSE
- Psycho- education and adherence counseling
- Assess side effects of medications
- Counseling and family involvement
- Counseling on alcohol and substance use issues
- Refill medications as indicated.
- Refer to Doctor led service once in 6 months for review | **Step 2: General Hospital or Health Centre** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Failure step1
- Bipolar I Disorder moderate symptoms
- Bipolar II Disorder moderate symptoms | - Vital signs, physical examination and MSE
- Psycho- education and adherence counseling
- Assess side effects of medications
- Counseling and family involvement
- Counseling on alcohol and substance use issues
- Review patients’ medications as indicated or refer | **Step 3: National Psychiatric Referral Hospital** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Failure at step 2
- Acute/severe symptoms of Bipolar I Disorder | - Refer to Doctor led services at the National Psychiatric Referral Hospital |

- A disturbance develops over a short period of time and fluctuates in severity during the course of a day.
- PLUS disturbance in cognition (memory deficit, disorientation, language challenges etc.)

text:
### TABLE 18: STEPWISE MANAGEMENT OF SUBSTANCE-RELATED AND ADDICTIVE DISORDERS **Step 1: Community Clinic Level** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Alcohol or substance use disorder; mild
- Substance or medication induced mental disorders; mild | - Screen and assess for social and legal issues as well as physical and psychiatric conditions
- Provide advice and counselling on behavior change as indicated
- If there is no improvement after 3 months, go to step 2 | **Step 2: General Hospital or Health Centre** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Failure at step1
- Alcohol or substance withdraw without perceptual disturbance
- Alcohol or substance use disorder; moderate
- Substance or medication induced mental disorders; moderate
- Substance or alcohol intoxication; moderate | - Screen, assess for social and legal issues, physical & psychiatric conditions
- Comprehensive assessment and management
- Counselling on behavior change
- Link with support groups: NA, AA
- If there is no improvement after 3 months, go to step 3 | **Step 3: National Psychiatric Referral Hospital** | Entry point | Management | | --- | --- | | - Failure at step 2
- Alcohol or substance withdraw with perceptual disturbance
- Severe alcohol or substance use disorder
- Substance induced mental disorders; severe
- Substance or alcohol intoxication; severe | Refer to Doctor, Clinical Psychologist, OT, SUD counselor/addiction professional led services |

### TABLE 19: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF CHILDHOOD PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the child has 3 or more of the following:
Deficits in intellectual functioning such as reasoning, judgment, planning, academic learning and learning from experience.
• Deficit in adaptive functioning such as communication, social participation and independent living.
• Onset of signs is during the developmental period (within the first 2 years of life). | INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY | • Provide counselling to parent(s) or caregiver(s)
• Provide psychoeducation about the condition
Refer to Job Aid; Developmental Disorders. Page 94
• Occupational therapy for behavioral modification
• Advice to teachers | | If the child has:
• Persistent difficulties in acquisition and use of language such as limited vocabulary, poor sentence construction and impairments in expression of written and spoken communication.
• Language abilities are substantially and quantifiably below those expected for age in communication, social participation and academic performance.
• Onset of signs is during the early developmental period.
• Difficulties not attributable to sensory impairment, motor dysfunction, medical, neurological condition or mental disorder. | LANGUAGE DISORDER | • Provide counselling to parents(s) or caregiver
• Speech therapy | | If the child has: - Persistent difficulties with speech sound production. - The disturbance causes limitations in effective communication, poor social participation, and academic achievement. - Onset of signs is during the early developmental period. - It is not attributable to congenital or acquired conditions. | SPEECH SOUND DISORDER | - Provide counselling to parents(s) or caregiver - Speech therapy | | If the child has one or more of the following: - Deficits in social communication and interaction in multiple contexts. - Restricted repetitive and stereotyped patterns of behavior, interests and activities. - Onset of signs is during the early developmental period. - Significant clinical impairments in social, academic and other areas of functioning. - Disturbances not attributable to intellectual disability. | AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER | - Assessment - Screen for ADHD, epilepsy, intellectual disability and manage as indicated - Provide counselling to parent(s) or caregiver(s) - Provide psychoeducation about the condition - Occupational therapy for behavioral modification - Advice to teachers Refer to Job Aid; Developmental Disorders. Page 94 | | If the child has 6 or more of the following symptoms of inattention that have persisted for at least 6 months. Inattention - Fails to give close attention to details. - Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly - Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish tasks - Forgetful in daily activities - Difficulties in organizing tasks and activities - Avoids tasks that require sustained mental effort - Easily loses things necessary for tasks or activities - Often forgetful in daily activities - Easily distracted 6 or more of the following past 6 months Hyperactivity-Impulsivity - Fidgets with hands and feet - Difficulty in awaiting turn - Runs about or climbs excessively in inappropriate situations - Leaves seat in situations in which remaining seated is expected. - Talks excessively - Interrupts or intrudes on others - Blurts out answers before question is completed - Difficulty playing quietly Onset of symptoms by age 12. Symptoms must be present in two or more settings (e.g school and home). | ATTENTION DEFICIT HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER (ADHD) | - Provide counselling to parents(s) or caregiver Refer to Job Aid; ADHD. Page 92 - Occupational therapy for behavioral modification - Advice to teachers - Prescribe psycho-stimulants or refer. Refer page 72 | | If the child has difficulties learning and using academic skills and has one of the following symptoms that have persisted for at least six months: - Inaccurate, slow and effortful word reading - Difficulty understanding the meaning of what is read. - Difficulty with spelling - Difficulties with written expression. - Difficulties with mathematical reasoning. - Difficulties with activities of daily living. Academic skills are substantially and quantifiably below those expected for age in communication, social participation and academic performance. Onset is during school age years. It may manifest prior to school age years Learning difficulties are not attributable to intellectual disability, medical, neurological, other mental and psychological disorders, or inadequate educational instruction | SPECIFIC LEARNING DISORDER | - Provide counselling to parents(s) or caregiver - Occupational therapy - Educational psychologist - Advice to teachers Refer to Job Aid; Developmental Disorders. Page 94 | The ADHD signs run over a page break (p.64); they are one cell here. Page references are the guide's printed page numbers.

### TABLE 19 (continued): enuresis, encopresis, oppositional defiant disorder and conduct disorder | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the child has the following symptoms:
Repeated involuntary or intentional voiding of urine in bed or clothes.

Frequency must be at least twice a week for three consecutive months or significant clinical distress that may show in impairments in social and academic performance.

Onset is at least age 5 years.
Behaviour is not attributable to substance use, or any medical, neurological or mental disorder. | ENURESIS |
• Assess for depressive symptoms
• Provide counselling
• Provide psychoeducation to parent(s) or caregiver
Asses for depressive symptoms. Refer to page 4 | | If the child has the following symptomssymptoms
Repeated involuntary or voluntary passage of faeces into inappropriate places.

Occurs at least once a month for at least three months.

Onset is at least age 4 years.
Behaviour is not attributable to substance use, or any medical, neurological or mental disorder. | ENCOPRESIS |
• Assess for depressive symptoms
• Provide counselling
• Provide psychoeducation to parent(s) or caregiver
Asses for depressive symptoms. Refer to page 4 | | If the child has a pattern of angry/ irritable, argumentative/defiant, or vindictiveness lasting at least six months as evidenced by at least four symptoms from any of the following categories and exhibited during interaction with at least one individual who is not a sibling: Angry irritable mood - Often loses temper - Often touchy and easily annoyed - Often angry and resentful Argumentative or defiant behaviour - Often argues with authority figures - Often defies or refuses to comply with rules - Often deliberately annoys others - Often blames others for his/her mistakes or behaviour Vindictiveness - Has been spiteful or vindictive at least twice within past six months Impacts negatively on social, educational and other areas of functioning. Behaviours are not attributable to a psychotic, substance use, depressive, or bipolar disorder | OPPOSITIONAL DEFiant DISORDER | - Provide counselling/ psychotherapy to parents(s) or caregiver - Advice to teachers - Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy Refer to Job Aid; Conduct Disorder Page 92 | | If the child has a repetitive and persistent pattern of behaviour in which basic rights of others or societal norms and rules are violated as manifested by at least three of the following in the past 12 months, with at least one criterion present in the past 6 months: - Violation of basic rights of others and societal norms - Aggression to people and animals. - Destruction of property - Deceitfulness or theft - Serious violation of rules. Disturbance in behaviour causes clinically significant impairment in social, and academic functioning. Onset is on the early preschool years. If the individual is age 18 years or older, criteria are not met for antisocial personality disorder. | CONDUCT DISORDER | - Provide counselling/ psychotherapy to parents(s) or caregiver - Advice to teachers - Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy |

text:
### Tables 21-22. First-line (amitriptyline, fluoxetine, sertraline) and second-line (duloxetine) antidepressants for major depressive disorder: doses, titration, maximum doses

**Table 21 - First line: tricyclic antidepressants**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amitriptyline po | Initial dose 25 mg for 3 days, then 50 mg | Bedtime | Short to long-term | 150-200 mg/day | A E |
| Then increase the dose gradually by 25 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Table 21 - First line: SSRIs (alternative)**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fluoxetine po | Initial dose 10-20 mg | Once daily | Short to long-term | 60-80 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 10-20 mg at an interval of 4-8 weeks if there is no response. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Sertraline po | Initial dose 25-50 mg | Bedtime | Short to long-term | 200 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 25-50 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Table 22 - Second line: SNRI**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duloxetine po | Initial dose 20-30 mg | Once daily | Short to long-term | 120 mg/day | S E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 20-30 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Note:** Amitriptyline is better prescribed if sedation is desirable. Fluoxetine and sertraline are better if sedation is not desirable, and for depression with suicidality, the elderly, children and frail physically ill patients.

heading_path: Chapter 4: Job Aids for Different Psychiatric Conditions > Pharmacological Management of Major Depressive Disorders > Insomnia and Psychotic Symptoms
text:
### Tables 23-24. Major depressive disorder: lorazepam for insomnia; antipsychotics (haloperidol, risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole) for depression with psychosis – doses and titration; cautions for SSRIs and TCAs

**Table 23 - Insomnia in major depressive disorder**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lorazepam po | 1-2 mg | Bedtime | 5-7 days | 2 mg | B E |

**Table 24 - Depressive disorder with psychosis: prescribe antidepressants concurrently with one antipsychotic**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haloperidol po | Initial dose 1.5-3 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 20 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 1.5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Risperidone po | Initial dose 1-2 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 6 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 50-200mg [as printed] if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Olanzapine po | Initial dose 5-10 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 25 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Aripiprazole po | Initial dose 2-5 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 30 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 5-10 mg if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Note:** Caution: SSRIs may cause agitation and an increased suicide risk during the first 2-4 weeks. TCAs can be fatal in overdose – conduct a suicide risk assessment at every follow-up visit and avoid them in patients with suicidal thoughts/attempt as much as possible. Avoid TCAs in children, the elderly and patients with heart disease, urinary retention, glaucoma and epilepsy. For depression with psychomotor agitation consider amitriptyline if no other contraindications; consider sertraline/fluoxetine for depression with psychomotor retardation.

text:
### TABLE 25: SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS: Table 25: Special Considerations in the Management of Major Depressive Disorders (Special case, Intervention)

TABLE 25: SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS

| Special case | Intervention |
| --- | --- |
| If younger than 12 years | • No antidepressants, provide counselling then refer |
| Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers | • Antidepressants should be avoided as far as possible and the refer |
| Depression with psychotic symptoms | • Prescribe anti-depressants + anti-psychotics |
| BAD, depressive phase. | • Prescribe mood stabilizer + anti-depressant + antipsychotic |
| If symptoms of mania emerge during treatment of depression | • Immediately stop antidepressants and refer |

text:
### Tables 30-31. Maintenance treatment of schizophrenia: first-line antipsychotics (haloperidol, sulpiride, chlorpromazine, aripiprazole) and second-line (risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine) – doses, titration, maximums; cautions

Maintenance phase: short- to long-term management after controlling agitation by rapid neuroleptization.

**Table 30 - First-line antipsychotics**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haloperidol po | Initial dose 1.5-5 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 20 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 1.5-5 mg at an interval of 3-14 days if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Sulpiride po | Initial dose 50-200 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 800 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 50-200 mg if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Chlorpromazine po | Initial dose 50-200 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 800 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 7-14 days by 50-200 mg if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Aripiprazole po | Initial dose 10-15 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 30 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 5-10 mg if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Risperidone po | Initial dose 1-2 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 6-8 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 0.5-2 mg at an interval of 3-14 days if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Olanzapine po | Initial dose 5-10 mg | Once to twice a day | Long term | 25 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 5 mg at a time if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Quetiapine po | Initial dose 25 mg | Once to twice a day | Short term | 750 mg/day | C E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 7-14 days by 50-100 mg increments until the mood is stabilised. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

### Table 35. Antimuscarinics prescribed with depot antipsychotics to prevent EPSE: trihexyphenidyl (Artane) or biperiden 2 mg daily; treatment duration and cautions for antipsychotics

| Medicine | Initial dose | Frequency | Duration | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trihexyphenidyl (Artane) po | 2 mg | Morning daily | Short to long term | A V |
| OR | OR | OR | OR | OR |
| Biperiden hydrochloride po | 2 mg | Morning daily | Short to long term | A V |

**Note:** Treatment duration: reduce the antipsychotic dose at each follow-up visit if mentally stable; maintain the lowest dose; consult a psychiatrist about discontinuing; if more than 3 episodes of psychosis, advise lifelong treatment. Caution: prescribe olanzapine and risperidone cautiously to the elderly and people with obesity, diabetes, hypertension or other cardiovascular conditions; one antipsychotic at a time, starting low and increasing gradually to an optimum dose for at least 4-6 weeks before considering it ineffective; treat side effects – do not provide an anticholinergic to every patient.

source_flags: Lamotrigine: '25-50 mg daily for the first 7 days then 50 mg 12-hourly' is faster than the recommended titration (25 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 50 mg daily for 2 weeks, then increase), which raises the risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
'Mood Stabilizerers' heading; lithium, the reference mood stabiliser, is not listed.

Lamotrigine titration (25-50 mg daily for 7 days, then 50 mg 12-hourly, increasing every 7-14 days) is faster than the usual schedule (25 mg daily for 2 weeks, 50 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 100 mg); fast titration raises the risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and doses must be halved with valproate. The maximum for bipolar disorder is usually 200-400 mg/day.
Sodium valproate is recommended without a caution about women and girls of childbearing potential (teratogenicity); lithium is not listed.

text:
### TABLE 52: SUMMARY OF MEDICATIONS FOR MANAGING THIAMINE DEFICIENCY SECONDARY TO ALCOHOL INTOXICATION

| Severity | Medications |
| --- | --- |
| Severe cases presenting with Wernicke’s encephalopathy | Thiamine 200-500mg IV/IM 8 hourly for 3-5 days, followed by 250-1000mg/day po for a month. |
| High risk patients of thiamine deficiency | Thiamine 200-500mg IV/IM 12 hourly for 3-5 days, followed by 250-300mg/day po for a month. |
| Patients with mild symptoms of thiamine deficiency | Thiamine 100mg po daily for a month. |

heading_path: Appendices > Appendix II: Depression Screening Form PHQ-9 > Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores
text:
### Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores (Score, Recommended Actions)

Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores

| Score | Recommended Actions |
| --- | --- |
| 0-4 | Normal range or full remission. The score suggests the patient may not need depression treatment. |
| 5-9 | Minimal depressive symptoms. Support, educate |
| 10-14 | Major depression, mild severity. Use clinical judgment about treatment, based on patient's duration of symptoms and functional impairment. Treat with antidepressant or psychotherapy. |
| 15-19 | Major depression, moderate severity. Warrants treatment for depression, using antidepressant, psychotherapy or a combination of treatment. |
| 20 or higher | Major depression, severe severity. Warrants treatment with antidepressant and psychotherapy, especially if not improved on monotherapy; follow frequently. |
